newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Motta sets out schedule for Telebras sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Motta sets out schedule for Telebras sale.

text.p: The Brazilian government plans to publish tender details for consultants to advise on the privatization of federal telecoms holding Telebras on October 30, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.
Motta told a news conference a government timetable for Telebras' sale also calls for the signing of at least one consultancy contract on December 30.
"Within three months and a bit, we will be launching the tender document or documents for the privatization of the Telebras system," Motta said.
He added that the government had not yet decided on the number of regional units Telebras would be broken into prior to privatization.

Officials have said previously that the company could be broken into four regional units and long-distance carrier Embratel but Motta said: "Today we are reopening this discussion, with a view of reducing the number of units."
The minister added the government would seek to avoid stifling competition by significantly cutting the number of units to be sold.
Motta was speaking after a meeting of the Interministerial Special Supervisory Committee for the privatization of Telebras, which is overseeing the multi-billion sale.
He reiterated that the government expects to reap more than $100 billion from the sale.
